questions.question: Discuss the laws of motion and their application.
questions.solution_html:
• Ans
  • Newton’s First Law (Law of Inertia)
  • A body remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force.
  • Application: A football remains still until kicked.
  • Newton’s Second Law (Law of Acceleration)
  • Force = Mass × Acceleration (F = ma).
  • Application: The harder a player kicks a ball, the faster it moves.
  • Newton’s Third Law (Action–Reaction)
  • For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
  • Application: When a swimmer pushes water backward with their arms and legs, the water pushes the
  • swimmer forward
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the historical development of kinesiology from ancient times to the modern era.
questions.solution_html:
• Ans
  • Kinesiology is the study of movement behaviour of all living organisms. The word kinesiology derived
  • from two Greek words. Kinein - to move, logos - To discourse or study. The study of kinesiology
  • began in ancient Greece, where scholars like Aristotle and Hippocrates studied human movement
  • and anatomy to understand health and performance. During the Renaissance, scientists such as
  • Leonardo da Vinci and Galileo Galilei analyzed body mechanics using observation and measurement.
  • In the 19th century, advances in anatomy and physiology gave kinesiology a scientific base. In the
  • 20th century, with the development of biomechanics, exercise physiology, and motor learning
  • kinesiology evolved into a distinct scientific discipline. Today, it integrates modern tools such as
  • motion analysis, electromyography, and computer modeling to improve health, fitness, and athletic
  • performance.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Discuss the importance of supination and pronation movements in daily activities.
questions.solution_html:
• Ans
  • Supination is the outward rotation of the forearm or foot, while pronation is the inward rotation. In the
  • forearm, these movements allow the palm to face up (supination) or down (pronation). They are
  • essential in everyday actions such as turning a doorknob, using a screwdriver, typing, eating, or
  • carrying objects. In the lower limb, controlled pronation and supination help with balance, shock
  • absorption, and efficient walking or running. Proper coordination of these movements prevents
  • injuries and supports smooth motor function in daily life and sports.
questions.final_answer: injuries and supports smooth motor function in daily life and sports
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Discuss the importance of the hip flexors and gastrocnemius muscles in daily activities.
questions.solution_html:
• Ans
  • The hip flexors (including the iliopsoas, rectus femoris, and sartorius) are responsible for lifting the
  • thigh toward the body. They play a key role in walking, running, climbing stairs, and sitting. Weak hip
  • flexors can cause poor posture and movement inefficiency.
  • The gastrocnemius, located in the calf, assists in plantar flexion of the foot (pointing the toes) and
  • flexion of the knee. It is vital for pushing off the ground while walking, running, or jumping. Together
  • these muscles ensure mobility, stability, and balance during everyday and athletic activities.
questions.final_answer: these muscles ensure mobility, stability, and balance during everyday and athletic activities
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025
